text:
Mark O'Neill: Quick sync — ACME POC scoping. Need to align ramp plan, success criteria, and who’s on-call for the test window. 6-week runway proposed.

Raj Patel: I can own SE coverage for weeks 1–3 for integration and prompt tuning. Can we clarify demo vs eval pass definitions?

Emma Chen: Pricing question from procurement: can we offer a 30k credit for a 6-week pilot, or do we need a different structure? cc @Mark O'Neill

Mark O'Neill: @Emma let's do a blended credit + success-based invoice. I want the POC acceptance criteria nailed down before we commit credits.

Lina Gomez: From our side, success = 1) >85% intent match on 3 core flows, 2) median latency < 400ms, 3) cost per 1k tokens < $1.50 during steady-state. Is that measurable from your dashboard?

Raj Patel: Yep — Console has token/cost breakdown per route and latency percentiles. We'll instrument three eval endpoints to map to your flows. Also recommend a small eval harness: 300 prompts per flow, seeded + live.

Mark O'Neill: Good. Can you draft a minimal deliverables list? I want clear handoffs for prompts/evals, logs, and rollback plan.

Raj Patel: Draft below, happy to iterate:
```
- Week 0: Kickoff, SSO + network checks, security questionnaire handed to SecOps
- Week 1: Integration + baseline eval (seeded prompts)
- Week 2: Prompt tuning + model variant testing (quantized vs fp16)
- Week 3: Load test, caching config, latency tuning
- Week 4: Customer-driven live evals, quality review
- Week 5: Final regression eval, cost review, runbook handoff
- Week 6: Acceptance demo + knowledge transfer
```

Emma Chen: That looks solid. For the security questionnaire, we’ll need answers within 3 business days after kickoff. Is SecOps on the thread? If not, open a ticket.

redwood-deploy-bot: New ticket created: #POC-ACME-512 — network whitelist + SecOps questionnaire assigned to secops-team.

Lina Gomez: For the eval prompts, can you accept a CSV? We have contextual history per example. Also need a way to redact PHI before upload.

Raj Patel: CSV is fine. We'll share a small uploader page with client-side redaction script. For PHI we recommend the provided scrubber and a manual review step.

Mark O'Neill: Who's the engineering standby for weeks 2–4 if we hit model OOMs or unexpected latency spikes?

Raj Patel: Assigning myself + one infra engineer (TBD). I'll list names in the runbook by EOD.

Emma Chen: Procurement also asks: if we exceed the 6-week window due to integrations, what's the extension pricing? Propose pro-rata daily rate based on committed credits.

Mark O'Neill: Agree pro-rata. I'll draft a short addendum to the SOW.

Lina Gomez: Final ask — can we get a simple success-checklist we can sign off on? That makes internal approvals easier.

Raj Patel: I'll produce a 1-page acceptance checklist tied to the 3 metrics (intent match, latency, cost) + deliverables. Will share by tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Mark O'Neill: Perfect. Action items: Raj — runbook + checklist by EOD tomorrow; Emma — pricing addendum draft; SecOps — answer questionnaire within 3 business days; Lina — upload seeded prompts CSV when uploader ready.

Lina Gomez: Thanks all. Looking forward to starting next Monday.

Emma Chen: Noted, I'll confirm credit structure today.

redwood-deploy-bot: Reminder: kickoff meeting scheduled Mon 10:00 AM PST — calendar invite sent to participants.
